item.title: PDP expels two Gombe chieftains over anti-party activities
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has expelled two of its chieftains in Gombe State, Hon. Khamisu Ahmed Mailantarki and Hon. Usman Aliyu Garry, over alleged anti-party activities and gross misconduct. The decision means the two politicians have lost their membership of the party and all rights and privileges accruing to them, following disciplinary proceedings over alleged actions the PDP said were capable of bringing it into disrepute. The PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, announced the expulsion in a statement, saying it followed the findings of the party’s Disciplinary Committee and consideration by relevant party organs. According to the statement, the offences against the two members fell under Sections 58(1)(a), (b), (h) and (j) of the party’s 2017 amended constitution, covering misconduct and activities considered detrimental to the party. The party maintained that the disciplinary process complied with the right to fair hearing under Section 57(6) of its constitution and Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution. Invoking Section 59(1)(j) of its constitution, the PDP declared that Mailantarki and Garry had ceased to be members and would no longer enjoy any affiliation, rights or privileges within its structures. Reaffirming the supremacy of its constitution, the party warned that members’ status would not shield them from disciplinary action. “No member, regardless of status, is above the Party’s laws and disciplinary framework,” the PDP stated. The party also stressed that its constitution remained binding on every member, regardless of position or standing within its structures. “The Party reiterates that its Constitution remains supreme and binding on all members,” it added. The PDP urged its members to remain loyal, disciplined and committed to its ideals, while working collectively to strengthen the party at all levels. item.title: Full list: Africa missing as UK releases 2026 list of universities for graduate work visa
item.description: The United Kingdom, UK has released its 2026 Global Universities List for the High Potential Individual (HPI) visa, naming universities across the world whose graduates may qualify for a route to live and work in the country, with no African institution appearing on the list. The list, published by the UK Home Office on November 1, 2026, covers qualifications awarded between November 1, 2026, and October 31, 2027. It includes institutions in countries such as the United States, Australia, China, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Germany, France and the Netherlands. The HPI visa is designed for recent graduates of eligible universities outside the UK. It allows qualifying applicants to come to Britain to work or look for work without first securing a job offer or employer sponsorship. However, being a graduate of an institution on the list does not automatically guarantee a visa. Applicants must also meet other immigration requirements, including English-language and financial criteria. The 2026 Global Universities List The Home Office’s 2026 list is presented below, with each institution’s country or territory as stated in the official publication. The institutions are spread across several regions, although North America and Asia account for a substantial share of the entries. The United States has the largest representation, with universities including Harvard University, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Stanford University, Yale University, Princeton University and the University of California system. Asian institutions on the list include Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Zhejiang University, Seoul National University, KAIST, Kyoto University and the National University of Singapore. Australia is represented by the Australian National University, Monash University, the University of Melbourne, the University of New South Wales and the University of Queensland, among others. No university from Nigeria or any other African country features in the 2026 publication. They demanded formal acknowledgement of their disassociation from the unauthorized JNPSNC press release of 30 October 2026, an end to presenting the statement as the collective position of all public service trade unions and respect for the TUC’s rejection of the inadequate N70,000 transport intervention and a demand for salary increment. The also demanded for recognition and representation of their unions in relevant public service negotiating structures, an end to issuing statements or taking decisions in the name of unions without consultation and express authorization. They called for respect for the independence and representative rights of all registered trade unions. The three unions said trade union unity cannot be imposed through exclusion, procedural manipulation or the silencing of constituent unions. You cannot negotiate workers’ welfare while denying their unions the right to representation.” They called on the Federal Government and relevant negotiating authorities to address the exclusion and ensure that all negotiating structures operate strictly within their established mandates. item.title: Atiku slams Tinubu over retired police officers’ pension crisis
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has again accused President Bola Tinubu of abandoning retired police officers to a failing pension system, despite their years of service protecting Nigerians. Atiku said it was unacceptable that officers who risked their lives to keep the country safe now had to stage daily protests at the National Pension Commission, PenCom, to demand the benefits they earned in service. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku described the situation as disgraceful, questioning how a government that deploys police officers to protect the powerful could fail to secure their welfare after retirement. “If police officers who served this country must endure humiliation to demand a fair pension, what hope is there for other Nigerians who have spent their working lives in public service?” he asked. The ADC presidential candidate said he was troubled by the protests and had directed his team to meet with the affected officers to hear their grievances firsthand. He also faulted Tinubu for failing to act on the Police Exit Bill, which, according to the statement, had remained on the President’s desk since March. Atiku accused the administration of treating police officers as expendable, recalling that many spent their careers protecting Nigerians, including political office holders, only to be abandoned when they needed government support most. To address the situation, he said his proposed Police Dignity Guarantee Plan would prioritise the welfare and retirement security of law enforcement personnel through prompt action on the Police Exit Bill, restoration of gratuity for police officers and implementation of the Police Pension Board Bill. “Insecurity cannot be defeated while those who protect the country are denied security in retirement. My Police Dignity Guarantee Plan will ensure that officers who serve Nigeria are properly supported throughout their careers and are not abandoned when they retire,” Atiku said. He pledged to implement the Police Pension Board Bill within 30 days of taking office, adding that his administration would seek to make Nigeria affordable again and restore dignity to those who had devoted their lives to national service. item.title: ‘Give Regina breathing space,’ Ned Nwoko appeals to fans, threatens legal action
item.description: Senator Ned Nwoko has appealed to the public, particularly fans and friends of his estranged wife, Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, to give her space to recover, warning that those spreading false reports about her could face legal action. Nwoko made the appeal in a statement shared on his Instagram page, expressing concern over what he described as the circulation of fabricated death announcements, misleading reports and hurtful content about the actress. He said the appeal was not only for Daniels but also for their children, who, according to him, deserve to see their mother supported and given every opportunity to recover. “I want to make a sincere appeal to the public, particularly Regina’s fans, friends, bloggers and social media commentators, to please give Regina some breathing space,” he said. The senator said Daniels had been through a lot and needed love, support and an opportunity to heal rather than public criticism. “Regina has been through a lot, more than many people may realise, and right now, what she needs most is love, support and the opportunity to recover.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Senator Prince Ned Nwoko (@princenednwoko) He also referenced a video Daniels shared on her birthday, saying it offered a glimpse into some of the health challenges she had been dealing with. According to him, her situation should not be an opportunity for people to judge or vilify her. Nwoko further said her well-being had always been important to him, adding that concerns about her welfare contributed to the decision to bring aspects of their private situation into the public domain. He expressed particular concern over reports falsely announcing the actress’s death and other claims about her health and personal circumstances. “These things are not harmless social media engagement. Regina sees many of these posts, and they are deeply distressing. They do nothing to support her recovery, rather, they add to the burden she is already carrying,” he said. The lawmaker urged the actress’s supporters to discourage the spread of such reports rather than amplify them. He also warned bloggers and social media users against deliberately publishing false information about Daniels, particularly claims concerning her death, health and personal life. “We are documenting these publications, and anyone found responsible will be held accountable through the appropriate legal channels,” he said. Nwoko added that Daniels deserved the opportunity to recover without being subjected to fabricated reports and renewed public scrutiny. item.title: ‘Ongoing dialogue’ with China after Mbappe row – Liga chief Tebas
item.description: La Liga president Javier Tebas said Monday he is maintaining dialogue with Chinese authorities in an effort to defuse a row over Kylian Mbappe’s comments about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not air a single La Liga match this weekend, while Real Madrid’s win at Racing Santander on Sunday was also not shown on pay television in the country. In a clip from an interview with French show “The Bridge” which has since been taken down, Mbappe had said he was amused by an internet meme showing his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga apologised for the comment after a backlash in China, where mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo. “For now, we wait and see how the situation develops… because given how events have unfolded, everything depends on things calming down a bit, on all the mess easing,” Tebas told reporters at the World in Progress forum in Barcelona. “There will be ongoing dialogue — I’m speaking with the Chinese authorities, both in Madrid and in Beijing, and we’re going to wait.” People walk past a bus featuring French football star Kylian Mbappe for Dongpeng Beverage Group’s “Bushuila” electrolyte drink on a street in Shanghai on October 27, 2026. Kylian Mbappe was dropped on October 27 by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong. (Photo by Jade GAO / AFP) Tebas, who held a meeting with Chinese ambassador to Spain Yao Jing last week, highlighted several strong links between China and Spanish football which could help resolve the dispute. “We’ve had a strategy for several years now with the political and sporting authorities in China,” he explained. Tebas met Chinese State Councillor Shen Yiqin and a high-ranking delegation at Barcelona’s La Masia youth academy facilities in February, along with Barcelona president Joan Laporta. “With the president of China Media Group (the parent organisation of CCTV) we have a good agreement,” continued Tebas. “He’s been to La Liga, I’ve met with him (Shen Haixiong). Every time I travel to Beijing I have a meeting with him.” China effectively cut ties with the NBA for several years from 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters, but Tebas said he was “hopeful” of reverting the current situation. “I’m going to travel, talk, and keep talking with the Chinese authorities,” he added. “We’ll try everything possible to normalise the situation as much as we can.” Mbappe scored on Sunday as Real Madrid beat Racing 3-0 in La Liga to move within three points of leaders Barcelona. item.title: NASS committed to increasing women’s participation — Bamidele
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, has said the 10th National Assembly is committed to removing barriers limiting women’s participation in governance through a proposed constitutional amendment seeking special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly. Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, said the proposed legislation was designed to address the persistent under-representation of women in Nigeria’s political institutions and ensure their participation in decisions affecting the country. He spoke as a guest speaker at the 2026 Law Week of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter, held in Ado-Ekiti, with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children”. The Senate Leader said the proposed constitutional alteration would create 37 additional seats in the Senate and 37 in the House of Representatives, with one seat reserved for women in each state and the Federal Capital Territory. item.content:encoded: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, has said the 10th National Assembly is committed to removing barriers limiting women’s participation in governance through a proposed constitutional amendment seeking special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly. Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, said the proposed legislation was designed to address the persistent under-representation of women in Nigeria’s political institutions and ensure their participation in decisions affecting the country. He spoke as a guest speaker at the 2026 Law Week of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter, held in Ado-Ekiti, with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children”. The Senate Leader said the proposed constitutional alteration would create 37 additional seats in the Senate and 37 in the House of Representatives, with one seat reserved for women in each state and the Federal Capital Territory. He added that the proposal also provided for three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, without displacing existing legislative seats. According to him, the arrangement is proposed to run for 16 years, covering four electoral cycles, after which its impact would be reviewed. Describing the initiative as a historic intervention rather than a partisan project, Bamidele said a democracy that excluded a significant proportion of its population from decision-making could not claim to be fully representative. He disclosed that the National Assembly had commenced engagements with State Houses of Assembly to secure the constitutionally required concurrence for the proposed amendment. He said the process was being pursued through extensive consultations and consensus-building. Bamidele, who commended the advocacy of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, said the 10th Assembly was determined to address historical gaps in women’s political representation. The lawmaker also identified globalisation, artificial intelligence, digitalisation, insecurity, economic instability and climate change as factors creating new challenges for women and children. He said women continued to face gender-based violence, economic exclusion, discrimination and inadequate healthcare, while children remained vulnerable to sexual abuse, trafficking, child labour, early marriage, malnutrition, educational deprivation and digital exploitation. He noted that poverty, unemployment, inadequate social protection, educational inequalities, social stigma and weak enforcement of existing laws had further compounded the challenges. Bamidele maintained that protecting women and children was not merely a humanitarian responsibility but a constitutional obligation and a critical investment in national development, economic productivity and social stability. He also highlighted legislative interventions of the 10th Assembly, including the four Tax Reform Acts of 2025, which he said exempted sanitary products, baby diapers and other essential products for women and children from Value Added Tax. He described the measure as a social justice intervention aimed at reducing the financial burden on low-income women and families. The Senate Leader urged FIDA to deepen its engagement with the National Assembly and other relevant institutions by identifying gaps in existing laws, proposing reforms and ensuring that government policies and budgetary provisions translated into tangible benefits for vulnerable Nigerians. He also challenged the organisation to hold the legislature accountable for implementing its commitments, particularly the proposed special seats for women and adequate funding for child protection, women’s healthcare and gender empowerment programmes. “A democracy that systematically excludes over half of its population from the decision-making tables that determine their future is, at best, a flawed democracy and, at worst, a veiled oligarchy. “The law is only as good as its implementation. Hold us accountable. Demand that the Special Seats Bill becomes law. Demand that appropriations for child protection and women’s health are not just passed, but released and utilised,” he said. In her keynote address, the Vice-Chancellor of Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti, Professor Smaranda Olarinde, called for stronger legal and institutional frameworks to protect women and children against emerging forms of abuse, particularly those enabled by technology and economic vulnerabilities. Olarinde said the growing use of artificial intelligence and digital platforms had created new threats, including cyberstalking, online harassment, deepfake images, impersonation and the exploitation of children. She called for stronger collaboration among government, the judiciary, law enforcement agencies, universities, religious and traditional leaders, the media and civil society organisations to tackle gender-based violence and child abuse. The vice-chancellor also urged FIDA to move beyond advocacy to measurable outcomes, proposing a collaborative Women and Children Access to Justice Action Framework to improve legal protection, digital safety and support for survivors. In his remarks, the Chief Judge of Ekiti State, Justice Ogunmoye, commended FIDA for selecting Bamidele to deliver the lecture, describing him as well placed to address emerging issues requiring legislative and policy reforms to protect women and children. Earlier, the Chairperson of FIDA, Ekiti State chapter, Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, said the organisation would remain committed to promoting, protecting and preserving the rights of women and children. She said changing realities continued to present new challenges to their safety, dignity and fundamental rights, requiring stronger laws, institutions and collective responses to ensure access to justice. item.title: FCT police arrest two suspected cable vandals in Guzape
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Operatives of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command have arrested two suspected members of a cable vandalism gang and recovered several cut-to-size armoured cables in Guzape, Abuja. The command’s spokesperson, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this on Monday, saying the arrests followed a routine surveillance patrol along Walter Ofonagoro Street, Guzape, in the early hours of October 31, 2026. Adeh said police operatives attached to Guzape Division, at about 1:30am, sighted a Lexus SUV and a Toyota Sienna parked under suspicious circumstances. She said the operatives approached the vehicles to ascertain the occupants’ reasons for being at the location, but the occupants sped off on sighting the police team, abandoning an accomplice who attempted to escape on foot. According to her, the operatives gave chase, intercepted and arrested the suspect. Preliminary investigations identified him as Sagir Abubakar of Kuchigoro Village, FCT, and allegedly linked him to a gang that targets secluded locations within the territory to vandalise public and private infrastructure. Adeh said a search of the surrounding premises where the suspects had been sighted led to the recovery of several armoured cables cut into pieces. She added that further investigations led to the arrest of another suspected accomplice, identified as Seidu Umar Bello, who had initially escaped in one of the vehicles. The police spokesperson said investigations were ongoing to establish the full extent of the suspects’ activities, identify other members of the gang and apprehend those still at large. She said the two suspects remained in custody and would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. The command urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest police station or through its emergency lines: 08032003913 and 08061581938. He defended the NLC’s handling of the controversial N70, 000 transport allowance secured from the Federal Government, insisting that the agreement was the product of collective bargaining and not a unilateral arrangement by the NLC. He also dismissed allegations that he was not a team player, declaring that the disagreements between the two labour centres should be examined based on facts rather than personal sentiments. The NLC President further questioned the TUC leadership’s commitment to workers’ interests, challenging its president over his alleged absence from Nigeria and the whereabouts of buses allocated to the organisation under the government’s compressed natural gas, CNG, transportation initiative. Usifo reacts In a swift reaction, President of TUC, Festus Osifo, disagreed with the stance of Joe Ajaero, maintaining, among others, that the NLC cannot negotiate the salaries and allowances of TUC members in the public service. However, speaking on the controversy surrounding the N70,000 transport allowance, Ajaero insisted that the agreement was negotiated with the Federal Government following an ultimatum issued by organised labour over the rising cost of living. He said the meeting that produced the agreement was attended by representatives of the Ministry of Labour, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, the Budget Office, the Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation. According to him, the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council was also represented at the meeting, with its secretary signing the agreement on behalf of the council. Ajaero said: “We issued an ultimatum to the government and were preparing to embark on industrial action. The government requested four days to meet with us at the Presidential Villa. “Following that meeting, agreements were reached.Every collective bargaining process produces an agreement. In this instance, the N70,000 transport allowance was included in the agreement. “I, therefore, do not understand the argument that the government simply gave us the money without any negotiation.” He further argued that the negotiating council had eight unions on its trade union side, seven affiliated with the NLC and one with the TUC, insisting that the presence and participation of the council’s representatives validated the agreement. Reacting to reports that some TUC-affiliated unions had rejected the allowance, Ajaero said such disagreements should be resolved internally within the affected organisations. He stated that the agreement was a matter of public record, adding that the signatories and organisations represented could be verified. On minimum wage On the allegation that he had promised to submit the NLC’s minimum wage proposals to the TUC but failed to do so, Ajaero described the claim as incorrect. He maintained that labour organisations were expected to submit their proposals directly to the appropriate minimum wage negotiating committee rather than through the media. According to him, public statements suggesting particular minimum wage figures should not be confused with formal submissions to a negotiating committee. He said: “You cannot present an organisation’s position as a formal submission to a minimum wage committee that has not yet been established. “It is when the committee resumes its work that each group will submit its proposal, supported by relevant justifications. You do not submit your proposal through the media,” he said. The NLC president also rejected the suggestion that workers should wait until the next minimum wage negotiations before receiving any form of financial relief, arguing that interventions were necessary to cushion the effects of inflation and the rising cost of living. He explained that salary increases must follow established collective bargaining procedures involving labour, employers and government. “There is a difference between his ideological orientation and mine. He comes from a capitalist perspective, while I come from the tradition of proletarian struggle and trade union leadership,” Ajaero said. He describing the disagreement between the two labour leaders as ideological rather than merely personal. The NLC President contended that government could not simply increase workers’ salaries without establishing an appropriate negotiating framework involving the Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association, NECA, labour representatives and government. He recalled that discussions on CNG transportation began during the previous NLC administration, when he served as Deputy President, adding that the union had advocated private-sector participation to ensure the success of the programme. However, he criticised what he described as excessive government control of the initiative, arguing that it had hindered its implementation. Turning the allegation against the TUC leadership, Ajaero questioned the whereabouts of the buses allocated to the organisation under the government’s transportation intervention. He said the NLC had received 90 buses and funding to support their fuel requirements for approximately 30 months, adding that the buses had been commissioned across different geopolitical zones. “Where are the 90 buses allocated to the TUC? Are they still operating, or have they developed wings?” he asked. He further questioned the TUC president’s participation in meetings connected with his responsibilities on the board of the National Pension Commission (PenCom), insisting that leadership positions in central labour organisations required a consistent presence in the country. Ajaero challenged the TUC president and the Nigerian Immigration Service to establish how much time he had spent in Nigeria during the year. He said: “You cannot live abroad while holding a leadership position in a central labour organisation. “The NLC president also denied claims that he had failed to maintain communication with his TUC counterpart, saying he had repeatedly attempted to reach him to harmonise their positions on minimum wage negotiations. According to Ajaero, he sent messages to the TUC president around June or July, proposing discussions on how both organisations could align their positions, but the proposed conversation never took place. He added that the TUC president had indicated that he was in transit and would return his call, but no further discussion followed. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Ismail Bala Muhammed, and Secretary, Mansur Ahmad, SSANU said the strike was triggered by the government’s failure to approve and implement the outstanding entitlements despite repeated engagements. The association said it initially submitted its demands through the appropriate channels before forwarding a comprehensive document on July 28, 2026, following the agreement between the Federal Government and the union on the 35 per cent Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA). It said it subsequently made several verbal and written appeals, including visits to the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry and the Deputy Governor, in a bid to secure an amicable settlement. Following the engagements, the state government constituted a committee comprising the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary, the Deputy Accountant-General and Professor Mustapha Aliyu to engage representatives of SSANU, the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT) and the Non-Academic Staff Union (NASU) from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education. At a meeting on October 9, the government communicated its position on the outstanding claims. However, SSANU said the response failed to address its members’ major concerns. According to the union, the government rejected payment of arrears arising from the 25 per cent salary increment, proposed implementing CONTTA from January 2027 subject to budgetary provision, and maintained that annual salary increments had already been implemented. Dissatisfied with the outcome, SSANU said it convened an emergency congress on October 13, where members resolved to issue a 14-working-day ultimatum to the government. The union warned that failure to meet its demands would trigger a five-day warning strike and potentially an indefinite industrial action. It, however, temporarily suspended the planned announcement of the strike after the Permanent Secretary scheduled a meeting with representatives of SSANU from SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education on October 14. At the meeting, the Permanent Secretary reportedly disclosed that the governor had directed the unions to resubmit their demands, separating existing claims from new ones and indicating their respective financial implications. The unions were also asked to distinguish between demands with lower and higher financial implications. Following deliberations, SSANU said it communicated its position to the Commissioner for Higher Education and formally suspended the implementation of its earlier resolution on October 15, while insisting that all outstanding demands must be approved and implemented. The association said it subsequently sent a reminder to the commissioner’s office on October 22, drawing attention to the approaching deadline. However, with the ultimatum expiring without what it considered concrete action, the union said it activated its earlier resolution and commenced the warning strike. SSANU is demanding payment of arrears arising from the 25 per cent salary increment, immediate approval and implementation of the 35 per cent CONTTA, annual salary increments for eligible members and release of outstanding check-off dues it alleged had been withheld. The union maintained that its demands were legitimate, arguing that the 35 per cent CONTTA was comparable to entitlements already approved and implemented for the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) at SSU and Shehu Shagari University of Education, as well as for teaching and non-teaching staff in other state-owned tertiary institutions, including the Polytechnic and College of Education. Describing the dispute as a case of unequal and discriminatory treatment, SSANU appealed to Governor Ahmed Aliyu to personally intervene and direct the immediate approval and implementation of the outstanding entitlements. It also called on relevant government agencies, traditional institutions, parents, students and other stakeholders to help facilitate an amicable resolution before the warning strike expires. The association warned that failure to resolve the dispute within the five-working-day period could result in a total and indefinite shutdown of services. It nevertheless reaffirmed its commitment to dialogue, industrial harmony and uninterrupted delivery of quality university education in the state, urging the government to replace further delays with concrete approvals and implementation measures. item.title: 2027: Niger Delta Youths slam Uzodinma’s aide over attack on Wike
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -A political group,Niger Delta Youth Movement, NDYM, has warned an aide to Governor Hope Uzodinma,Mr. Collins Opurozor,to stop attacking the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory,FCT, Nyesom Wike over the senatorial tussle between the Governor and Owelle Rochas Okorocha. The group also urged Opurozor not to use the disagreement between the two APC Chieftains to create hostility between the South East zone and Wike. The group alleged that Opurozor has been attempting to undermine Wike through inflammatory political remarks. The Movement declared that it would not continue to watch Opurozor attack the FCT Minister without consequences and urged him to exercise restraint and desist from using media interviews to settle political scores. In a statement by its Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jeffery Nwali, NDYM condemned Opurozor’s comments on a national television where he accused Wike of attempting to turn the South East into his personal political fiefdom by allegedly encouraging the emergence of weak leaders in the region to preserve his political influence. Describing the comments as reckless and provocative,the group,however, insisted that Wike’s political engagements should not be misrepresented as an attack on Igbo interests. The statement read;”We condemn the attempt by Collins Opurozor to drag the FCT Minister into Imo State’s political disputes, particularly following the Federal High Court judgment concerning Governor Uzodinma’s APC senatorial candidacy in Imo West senatorial zone. “Disagreements between Uzodinma and other political actors in Imo State should not be allowed to create unnecessary hostility between the South East and the FCT Minister. “During the television interview, Opurozor strongly criticized the judgment, dismissed Senator Samuel Anyanwu over what he described as his lack of grassroots support in Imo State, and berated the administration of former Governor Rochas Okorocha as too disgraceful to be remembered. “He also accused Wike of undermining Igbo political interests by allegedly supporting political figures opposed to Uzodinma. “Collins Opurozor is a young political aide who over- rates his intelligence and mistakes verbal aggression for political sophistication. Political disagreements should not become excuses to denigrate established political leaders.” The post 2027: Niger Delta Youths slam Uzodinma’s aide over attack on Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria targets wider access to West African markets
item.description: … FG urges businesses to exploit ECOWAS trade scheme By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja LOKOJA — The Federal Government has urged Nigerian manufacturers, farmers and entrepreneurs to take advantage of the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme (ETLS) to expand their businesses into West African markets. The government said increased regional trade was critical to economic growth, integration and stability across the sub-region. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the call at the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme Sensitisation Workshop for the North-Central zone, held in Lokoja, Kogi State, in collaboration with the ECOWAS Commission. Enikanolaiye disclosed that Nigeria had registered about 3,500 companies and 20,000 products under the scheme, but said the figures remained below the country’s potential compared with the performance of some other ECOWAS member states. He urged Nigerian businesses to exploit the scheme, which grants qualifying products originating from member countries preferential access to regional markets, to increase exports, expand production and improve the country’s competitiveness. The minister identified the agricultural potential of Kogi and other North-Central states as an opportunity to develop products for regional and international markets. He listed livestock, mangoes, millet, maize, sugar, groundnuts and cashew as commodities that could be processed into value-added products for export to other West African countries. Enikanolaiye urged participants to use the workshop to familiarise themselves with product registration procedures, rules of origin, certification and other requirements for accessing preferential markets under the scheme. “Expanding trade among African countries would not only promote economic cooperation but also strengthen relationships among nations and contribute to peace and security across the continent,” he said. The minister identified the agricultural potential of Kogi and other North-Central states as an opportunity to develop products for regional and international markets. He listed livestock, mangoes, millet, maize, sugar, groundnuts and cashew as commodities that could be processed into value-added products for export to other West African countries. Enikanolaiye urged participants to use the workshop to familiarise themselves with product registration procedures, rules of origin, certification and other requirements for accessing preferential markets under the scheme. “Expanding trade among African countries would not only promote economic cooperation but also strengthen relationships among nations and contribute to peace and security across the continent,” he said. The minister’s appeal comes as Kogi State seeks to position itself as a centre for regional commerce, industrial production and agricultural processing, leveraging its geographical location and natural resources. Welcoming participants, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo said the state’s location at the confluence of Rivers Niger and Benue, agricultural resources, solid mineral deposits and road networks connecting major economic centres offered significant opportunities for trade and investment. Ododo said his administration’s 32-year development plan was designed to translate these advantages into sustainable economic prosperity. He disclosed that the proposed Ajaokuta Free Trade Zone, Agro-Processing Zone and Kogi International Airport were among the strategic projects being pursued to attract investors, expand production capacity and connect local businesses to international markets. The governor also highlighted the Kogi Rebrand Initiative and Invest in Kogi campaign as efforts to showcase investment opportunities in agriculture, solid minerals, tourism and industrial development. He urged farmers, manufacturers, miners, processors and entrepreneurs in the state to look beyond the domestic market and prepare their products for consumers across West Africa, particularly in Accra, Abidjan, Lome and Cotonou. Ododo commended President Bola Tinubu for his economic reform agenda, saying policy consistency, local production and an enabling business environment were necessary to build a competitive economy. He assured that the state would continue to complement Federal Government initiatives through infrastructure development, investment promotion and enterprise support. Also speaking, the Secretary to the Kogi State Government, Dr Folashade Ayoade Arike, reaffirmed the state’s readiness to participate in international trade, describing regional market access as an opportunity to expand the commercial potential of local businesses. Ayoade identified the proposed international airport and the ongoing Lokoja International Market project as important infrastructure for facilitating the movement of goods and connecting businesses to wider markets. She appealed to the Federal Government to support the completion of critical infrastructure projects that would strengthen the state’s commercial capacity. The SSG also assured participants of the state government’s commitment to security, describing it as a fundamental requirement for successful business operations and investment.
